problem:
An irrigation tank initially holds $800\,\text{L}$ of water containing $1\,200\,\text{g}$ of dissolved fertilizer.
A solution containing $25\,\text{g/L}$ of dissolved fertilizer is pumped into the tank at a rate of $6\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $10\,\text{L/min}.$ Which differential equation best describes the amount of fertilizer $Q$ in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins?
worked_solution:
Since $Q$ is the mass of fertilizer in the tank at time $t,$ the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes. This is equal to the rate at which fertilizer enters the tank minus the rate at which fertilizer leaves the tank.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{g}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which fertilizer enters the tank.

First, note that a water solution containing $25\,\text{g/L}$ of fertilizer enters the tank at a rate of $6\,\text{L/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *fertilizer* enters the tank is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(25\,\frac{\text{g}}{\text{L}})\cdot (6\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(25\,\frac{\text{g}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot (6\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =150\,\frac{\text{g}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which fertilizer exits the tank.

Now, to find the rate at which fertilizer leaves the tank, we must first determine the volume of water in the tank at time $t.$

- The tank initially contains $800\,\text{L}$ of water.

- A solution enters the tank at a rate of $6\,\text{L/min}.$ So, after $t$ minutes, $6t\,\text{L}$ have entered the tank.

- The completely mixed water solution leaves the tank at a rate of $10\,\text{L/min}.$ So, after $t$ minutes, $10t\,\text{L}$ have left the tank.

As a result, the volume of water in the tank after $t$ minutes is 

$$
800+6t-10t=800-4t\,\text{L}.
$$

Since $Q$ is the amount of fertilizer in the tank, the *concentration* of the water solution at time $t$ is 

$$
\frac{Q}{800-4t}\,\frac{\text{g}}{\text{L}}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed water leaves at a rate of $10\,\text{L/min},$ *fertilizer* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(10\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{800-4t}\,\frac{\text{g}}{\text{L}}) \\  & =(10\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{800-4t}\,\frac{\text{g}}{\cancel{\text{L}}}) \\  & =\frac{10Q}{800-4t}\,\frac{\text{g}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

Finally, the rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =150-\frac{10Q}{800-4t}\end{aligned}
$$

which finally gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{10}{800-4t}Q=150.\end{aligned}
$$
